response.answer: Implement uncertainty with ensembles, temperature scaling, and isotonic regression; acceptable ECE bounds are typically below 0.1; incorporate uncertainty by using prediction intervals in decision-making.

results.title: A Primer on Uncertainty and Calibration in Deep Learning
results.content: For example, instead of saying: *“The house price is 480,000,”a well-calibrated model would say: “The price is 480,000 ± 70,000 , but I’m really not confident because the location is novel to me.” And that ± 70,000 is where uncertainty kicks in.* Hence, uncertainty in deep learning is the **lack of confidence a model has in its predictions**, typically arising from **incomplete information, ambiguous data, or limitations in the model itself** (this shouldn’t be confused with confidence value model gives as output, though ideally it should, this discrepancy in expected and actual behaviour of model logits/probability/scores is comes under model calibration, this also will be covered in latter sections). A deterministic model makes a point prediction `y=f(x`), but a probabilistic or uncertainty-aware model outputs a **distribution** over possible predictions: `y∼p(y∣x).` Uncertainty is then quantified via: * **Variance**, entropy, or confidence intervals in regression * **Predictive entropy** or margin in classification That said, lets start diving into core concepts. ### Method 1 : Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) This simplest way of modelling this type of uncertainty is by predicting not just a mean output `μ(x)` but also a corresponding variance `σ2(x)`, treating the output as a Gaussian distribution: \(y^∼N(μ(x),σ2(x))\) During training, we use *Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE)*, leading to the following Negative Log-Likelihood (NLL) loss: \(\mathcal{L}\_{\text{NLL}} = \frac{1}{2\sigma²(x)} (y -\mu(x))² + \frac{1}{2} \log \sigma²(x)\) This formulation naturally balances error (left term) and uncertainty (right term containing `σ)`. Conversely, a model may express confident predictions (low uncertainty) but be overconfident and hence **badly mis-calibrated**. #### Ensembles and Dropout Both methods, discussed earlier for epistemic uncertainty, naturally improve calibration: * **Ensembles** smooth out extreme predictions across models * **Dropout at test time** simulates stochastic ensembles These methods reduce **variance** and act as regularizers, especially useful when used with temperature scaling. #### Prediction Interval Plots For regression models, especially those predicting both mean and variance (e.g., heteroscedastic regression), we can plot: * Confidence intervals (e.g., 90%, 95%) This reveals how uncertainty expands or contracts with input domain shifts, and whether **the intervals actually cover the target**, which speaks to coverage and calibration.

results.title: uncertainty-calibration · PyPI
results.content: Utilities to calibrate model uncertainties and measure calibration. # Uncertainty Calibration Library. This repository contains library code to measure the calibration error of models, including confidence intervals computed by Bootstrap resampling, and code to recalibrate models. Our functions estimate the calibration error and ECE more accurately than prior "plugin" estimators and we provide Bootstrap confidence intervals. See Verified Uncertainty Calibration for more details. Motivating example for uncertainty calibration: Calster and Vickers 2015 train a random forest that takes in features such as tumor size and presence of teratoma, and tries to predict the probability a patient has testicular cancer. Calibration is a popular way to measure the quality of a model's uncertainties, and recalibration is a way to take an existing model and correct its uncertainties to make them better. This library focuses on calibration for classification tasks. Measuring the calibration error of a model is as simple as:. calibration_error = cal.get_calibration_error(model_probs, labels). Our library makes it very easy to measure confidence intervals on the calibration error as well, using bootstrap resamples. [lower, _, upper] = cal.get_calibration_error_uncertainties(model_probs, labels). ## Advanced: ECE, Debiasing, and Top-Label Calibration Error. By default, our library measure per-class, root-mean-squared calibration error, and uses the techniques in Verified Uncertainty Calibration to accurately estimate the calibration error. However, we also support measuring the ECE (Guo et al) and using older, less accurate, ways of estimating the calibration error. calibration_error = cal.get_ece(model_probs, labels). calibration_error = cal.get_top_calibration_error(model_probs, labels, p=1). Multiclass calibration vs ECE / Top-label: When measuring the calibration error of a multiclass model, we can measure the calibration error of all classes (per-class calibration error), or of the top prediction. ## Verified Uncertainty Calibration paper. This repository also contains code for the NeurIPS 2019 (Spotlight) paper Verified Uncertainty Calibration. * The calibration error of methods like Platt scaling and temperature scaling are typically underestimated, and cannot be easily measured. * We propose an efficient recalibration method where the calibration error can be measured. * Experiments showing the debiased estimator can estimate calibration error with fewer samples than standard estimator (Section 5). Details for the file `uncertainty-calibration-0..gz`. * Download URL: uncertainty-calibration-0..gz. Hashes for uncertainty-calibration-0..gz.

results.content: This guide:  Introduces the motivation for quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems  Explains important concepts in probability that relate to deep learning AWS Prescriptive Guidance – Quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems August 2020 Page 3 of 25  Demonstrates current state-of-the-art techniques for quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems, highlighting their associated benefits and limitations  Explores these techniques within the transfer learning setting of natural language processing (NLP)  Provides a case study inspired by projects performed in a similar setting As discussed in this guide, when quantifying uncertainty in deep learning, a good rule of thumb is to use temperature scaling with deep ensembles. AWS Prescriptive Guidance – Quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems August 2020 Page 8 of 25 Methods for estimating uncertainty in deep learning This section discusses three methods for quantifying uncertainty in deep learning networks, and provides general recommendations for using each method:  Temperature scaling  Monte Carlo dropout  Deep ensembles Temperature scaling In classification problems, the predicted probabilities (softmax output) are assumed to represent the true correctness probability for the predicted class. AWS Prescriptive Guidance – Quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems August 2020 Page 9 of 25 We recommend that you integrate the temperature scaling method as a part of the model training process: After a model training is completed, extract the temperature value T by using the validation dataset, and then rescale logit values by using T in the softmax function. AWS Prescriptive Guidance – Quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems August 2020 Page 14 of 25 Document coverage and accuracy ─ in domain We compared the predictive performance of deep ensembles with dropout applied at test time, MC dropout, and a naïve softmax function, as shown in the following graph. AWS Prescriptive Guidance – Quantifying uncertainty in deep learning systems August 2020 Page 19 of 25 Defining a decision rule To maximize the benefit of the results, we use the following ensemble rule: For each input, we take the model that has the lowest probability of being positive (acceptable) to make flagging decisions.
